headline: UCLA's Ground Game Overwhelms Oklahoma in Convincing Road Victory
body: UCLA dismantled Oklahoma 49-28 on Saturday, delivering a statement performance that hinged on one fundamental principle: control the line of scrimmage. The Bruins rushed for 201 yards on the ground while holding Oklahoma to just 46, a 155-yard gap that told the entire story of a one-sided afternoon. Duece Jones-Drew earned Player of the Game honors, but the real victory belonged to UCLA's offensive line, which created running lanes all day and allowed the Bruins to dictate tempo from the opening kickoff.

Oklahoma's passing attack showed occasional flashes through Glass, who completed 19 of 32 for 316 yards and three touchdowns, and Sater's 93-yard receiving performance kept the Sooners competitive on the scoreboard. But without a functioning ground game—Bernard managed only 22 yards on four carries—Oklahoma became predictable and one-dimensional. UCLA's defense, anchored by Barksdale's seven tackles and a sack, tightened the noose in the second half when it mattered most, forcing a turnover that sealed momentum.

The Bruins' balanced attack, led by Iamaleava's efficient 19-of-27 passing day and three touchdown passes, proved too much for Oklahoma to answer. Smith's 70-yard receiving line and the efficient deployment of four running backs created confusion for an Oklahoma defense that never recovered from UCLA's early dominance. This was not a game decided by individual brilliance but by superior execution and preparation—the kind of performance that separates contenders from pretenders down the stretch.
turningPoint: Oklahoma's lone turnover in the third quarter came on a critical drive that could have tightened the score; UCLA's subsequent touchdown made it 35-21 and effectively ended any realistic Sooner comeback.

unsungHero.name: Barksdale
unsungHero.why: Barksdale's seven tackles and sack were the backbone of UCLA's defensive dominance, setting the tone for run-stopping efficiency that forced Oklahoma into one-dimensional play, yet Jones-Drew's offensive visibility overshadowed the anchor of the win.
